q: that a group of Jinn attentively listened to me
(to their fellow Jinn when they returned to their places),
'Indeed we have heard a most astounding
v.s: Say, [O Muhammad], “It has been revealed to me that a group of the jinn listened and said, ‘Indeed, we have heard an amazing Qur’ān [i.e., recitation].
v.c: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “It has been revealed to me that a group of jinn listened ˹to the Quran,˺ and said ˹to their fellow jinn˺: ‘Indeed, we have heard a wondrous recitation.

q: ‘“It points towards righteousness so we believed in it and we shall never ascribe any partner to our Rabb.“'
v.s: It guides to the right course, and we have believed in it. And we will never associate with our Lord anyone.
v.c: It leads to Right Guidance so we believed in it, and we will never associate anyone with our Lord ˹in worship˺.

q: ‘“Most exalted is the majesty of our Rabb, Who has neither taken a wife nor a child.“'
v.s: And [it teaches] that exalted is the nobleness of our Lord; He has not taken a wife or a son
v.c: ˹Now, we believe that˺ our Lord—Exalted is His Majesty—has neither taken a mate nor offspring,

q: used to say things about Allaah that transgress the limit
(when they attributed partners and children to Allaah)...'”
v.s: And that our foolish one [i.e., Iblees] has been saying about God an excessive transgression.
v.c: and that the foolish of us used to utter ˹outrageous˺ falsehoods about Allah.

q: “...and we always thought that no human or Jinn could ever lie about Allaah.“'
(We did not expect humans and Jinn to be bold enough to lie about Allaah. Consequently, we accepted the practices of Shirk that they told us, assuming it to be correct. We now know better.)
v.s: And we had thought that mankind and the jinn would never speak about God a lie.
v.c: We certainly thought that humans and jinn would never speak lies about Allah.

q: (adding to our practices of Shirk was that)
there were those from mankind who
(when they stopped over at a frightening place during their travels, they would call out to the leaders of the Jinn at that place and implore them for protection from other Jinn. In doing so they)
used to seek protection from the Jinn and
(by making them feel that since others pleaded for assistance from them, they considered themselves to be too important and powerful to submit to Allaah).'”
v.s: And there were men from mankind who sought refuge in men from the jinn, so they [only] increased them in burden [i.e., sin].
v.c: And some men used to seek refuge with some jinn—so they increased each other in wickedness.

q: think that Allaah shall not resurrect anyone
(and because of this, they did not mend their ways).'”
v.s: And they had thought, as you thought, that God would never send anyone [as a messenger].
v.c: And those ˹humans˺ thought, just like you ˹jinn˺, that Allah would not resurrect anyone ˹for judgment˺.

q: have sought to reach the skies
(to eavesdrop on the conversations of the angels to learn about future events)
but found it filled with stern
(stars which the angels threw at any Jinn caught trying to eavesdrop).'”
v.s: And we have sought [to reach] the heaven but found it filled with powerful guards and burning flames.
v.c: ˹Earlier˺ we tried to reach heaven ˹for news˺, only to find it filled with stern guards and shooting stars.

q: we used to take up positions there
(once revelation has begun coming to Rasulullaah ﷺ)
whoever eavesdrops will find a flaming fire
v.s: And we used to sit therein in positions for hearing, but whoever listens now will find a burning flame lying in wait for him.
v.c: We used to take up positions there for eavesdropping, but whoever dares eavesdrop now will find a flare lying in wait for them.

q: (now that Allaah has sent Rasulullaah ﷺ)
is intended for those on earth
or whether their Rabb intends guidance for them
v.s: And we do not know [therefore] whether evil is intended for those on earth or whether their Lord intends for them a right course.
v.c: Now, we have no clue whether evil is intended for those on earth, or their Lord intends for them what is right.

q: ‘“Among us there are the righteous ones and those who are otherwise
v.s: And among us are the righteous, and among us are [others] not so; we were [of] divided ways.
v.c: Among us are those who are righteous and those who are less so. We have been of different factions.

q: ‘“We know that we are unable to escape
Allaah on earth and we shall never be able to escape from Him by fleeing
v.s: And we have become certain that we will never cause failure to God upon earth, nor can we escape Him by flight.
v.c: ˹Now,˺ we truly know that we cannot frustrate Allah on earth, nor can we escape from Him ˹into heaven˺.

q: it. Whoever believes in his Rabb has neither loss nor humiliation
(neither in this world nor in the Aakhirah).
v.s: And when we heard the guidance [i.e., the Qur’ān], we believed in it. And whoever believes in his Lord will not fear deprivation or burden.
v.c: When we heard the guidance ˹of the Quran˺, we ˹readily˺ believed in it. For whoever believes in their Lord will have no fear of being denied ˹a reward˺ or wronged.

q: are Muslims while some of us are oppressors
(Kuffaar, who oppress themselves by inviting Allaah's punishment by committing kufr).
Those who accept Islaam have surely sought the path of good.“'
v.s: And among us are Muslims [in submission to God], and among us are the unjust. And whoever has become Muslim - those have sought out the right course.
v.c: And among us are those who have submitted ˹to Allah˺ and those who are deviant. So ˹as for˺ those who submitted, it is they who have attained Right Guidance.

q: they shall be fuel for Jahannam.“'
v.s: But as for the unjust, they will be, for Hell, firewood.'
v.c: And as for the deviant, they will be fuel for Hell.’”

m: surely We (would) have given them to drink
q: (O Rasulullaah ﷺ! Say that revelation has also come to me to inform me that)
(Islaam), (then instead of punishing them with droughts,)
We shall definitely bless them with abundant showers
v.s: And [God revealed] that if they had remained straight on the way, We would have given them abundant rain [i.e., provision].
v.c: Had the deniers followed the Right Way, We would have certainly granted them abundant rain to drink—

q: (to ascertain whether they will express gratitude or not).
Whoever turns away from the remembrance of his Rabb
We shall enter him into a severe punishment.
v.s: So We might test them therein. And whoever turns away from the remembrance of his Lord He will put into arduous punishment.
v.c: as a test for them. And whoever turns away from the remembrance of their Lord will be admitted by Him into an overwhelming punishment.

q: (prostration and all other forms of worship)
are only for Allaah, so do not supplicate to
v.s: And [He revealed] that the masjids are for God, so do not invoke with God anyone.
v.c: The places of worship are ˹only˺ for Allah, so do not invoke anyone besides Him.

q: (to intimidate him so that he stops worshipping Allaah).
v.s: And that when the Servant [i.e., Prophet] of God stood up supplicating Him, they almost became about him a compacted mass."
v.c: Yet when the servant of Allah stood up calling upon Him ˹alone˺, the pagans almost swarmed over him.

q: (shall not be intimidated by you because I)
worship only my Rabb and I do not ascribe any as His partner.”
v.s: Say, [O Muhammad], “I only invoke my Lord and do not associate with Him anyone.”
v.c: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “I call only upon my Lord, associating none with Him ˹in worship˺.”

q: (When the Kuffaar challenge you to cause Allaah's punishment to come to them for opposing you, then)
“Indeed I have no power to do you any harm nor any good.”
(All this is only in Allaah's power)
v.s: Say, "Indeed, I do not possess for you [the power of] harm or right direction."
v.c: Say, “It is not in my power to harm or benefit you.”

q: (When they ask you to change parts of the Qur'aan to accommodate them so that they may incline towards Islaam, then)
Say, “Without doubt, none can ever protect me from Allaah
and I cannot find any refuge
v.s: Say, "Indeed, there will never protect me from God anyone [if I should disobey], nor will I find in other than Him a refuge.
v.c: Say, “No one can protect me from Allah ˹if I were to disobey Him˺, nor can I find any refuge other than Him.

q: (Also tell them that you are not obliged to force them to accept Islaam by saying to them,) “(My responsibility is nothing)
from Allaah and fulfilling His messages.
Whoever disobeys Allaah and His Rasool shall have the fire of Jahannam where they will live
v.s: But [I have for you] only notification from God, and His messages." And whoever disobeys God and His Messenger - then indeed, for him is the fire of Hell; they will abide therein forever.
v.c: ˹My duty is˺ only to convey ˹the truth˺ from Allah and ˹deliver˺ His messages.” And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger will certainly be in the Fire of Hell, to stay there for ever and ever.

q: (It appears from the attitude of the Kuffaar that they will never accept the truth of Islaam)
then will they realise who had the weakest assistant and whose numbers were fewer.

(In this world, the Kuffaar look down on the Muslims, thinking that the Muslims have weak allies and are fewer in number. However, the Kuffaar will realise the error of their judgement on the Day of Qiyaamah when the Muslims will emerge as the stronger ones and will have each other to intercede for them while the Kuffaar will have no allies to help them.)
v.s: [The disbelievers continue] until, when they see that which they are promised, then they will know who is weaker in helpers and less in number.
v.c: Only when they see what they have been threatened with will they know who is weaker in helpers and inferior in manpower.

q: Say, “I do not know whether what you have been promised
is near or whether your Rabb has specified a lengthy term for it
(are hence Qiyaamah will come only after a long period).”
v.s: Say, "I do not know if what you are promised is near or if my Lord will grant for it a [long] period."
v.c: Say, “I do not know if what you are promised is near or my Lord has set a distant time for it.

q: “He is the Knower of the unseen and He has informed no one about His unseen knowledge
(only Allaah has complete knowledge of the unseen)...
v.s: [He is] Knower of the unseen, and He does not disclose His [knowledge of the] unseen to anyone
v.c: ˹He is the˺ Knower of the unseen, disclosing none of it to anyone,

q: (certain aspects of this knowledge, such as the injunctions of Deen and certain other matters, which He has informed only)
(However, Allaah had not even informed Rasulullaah ﷺ when Qiyaamah will occur.)
(Rasulullaah ﷺ) and behind him (when he received revelation so that no one could interfere with the transmission of revelation)...
v.s: Except whom He has approved of messengers, and indeed, He sends before him [i.e., each messenger] and behind him observers
v.c: except messengers of His choice. Then He appoints angel-guards before and behind them

q: ...so that He may know that they have conveyed
He has knowledge of their conditions.
(He knows all about these angels He has placed on guard and has selected them because they are fit for the task)
and He keeps meticulous count of everything.
(He knows exactly how much of the Qur'aan has been revealed at any point of time during the lifetime of Rasulullaah ﷺ).
v.s: That he [i.e., Muhammad (صلى الله عليه وسلم)] may know that they have conveyed the messages of their Lord; and He has encompassed whatever is with them and has enumerated all things in number.
v.c: to ensure that the messengers fully deliver the messages of their Lord—though He ˹already˺ knows all about them, and keeps account of everything.”
